ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 5-4-5, on a platform scale there is placed a cup containing water, and a wooden small ball is tied to the bottom of the cup with a thin string. If the thin string suddenly breaks, during the process in which the small wooden ball floats up to the water surface, how does the reading of the platform scale change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, on the platform scale there is placed a cup containing water; inside the cup there is a small ball immersed in the water; the text states that the small ball is wooden and is tied to the bottom of the cup by a thin string. Then reason: regard the cup, water, and wooden ball as a whole. When the thin string has not broken and the system is at rest, the reading of the platform scale is equal to the total gravity of this whole. After the thin string breaks, the wooden ball floats upward because its density is less than that of water; when it floats upward, the volume originally occupied by the wooden ball must be filled downward by water, equivalent to the lighter wooden ball moving upward and the same volume but heavier water moving downward. For the whole of “cup + water + wooden ball,” the only external forces are gravity and the supporting force of the platform scale, so there is N-W=Ma_center of mass. During the upward-floating process, the effect of the heavier water moving downward predominates, making the whole center of mass have a downward acceleration; therefore the supporting force N of the platform scale is less than the total gravity W when at rest. The reading of the platform scale becomes smaller.
